column3: Close to the Hebrew; “from days to days” becomes “yearly,” and “to bow down” becomes “to worship.”
Close to the Hebrew; “and it was the day” is rendered as a habitual “whenever the time came.”
Close to the Hebrew; the Hebrew for “double portion” is uncertain in meaning, and NKJV turns “and” before “the LORD had closed” into “although.”
Close to the Hebrew; הֵיכַל (“temple, palace”) is rendered “tabernacle.”
NKJV renders “seed of men” as “a male child.”
Close to the Hebrew; “hard of spirit” becomes “of sorrowful spirit.”
NKJV renders “a daughter of worthlessness” (Belial) as “a wicked woman.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “saying” before Hannah’s words.
Close to the Hebrew; “the sacrifice of the days” is rendered “the yearly sacrifice.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the lad was a lad” is rendered “the child was young.”
NKJV renders the wordplay on שָׁאוּל (“asked”) as “lent,” and has “they worshiped” where the Hebrew has “he bowed down.”
